resources.string: Thin pancakes with a tender cottage cheese filling.
Mix flour, milk and eggs into a smooth batter.
Fry thin pancakes on both sides.
Wrap the cottage cheese in the pancakes.
Delicious pasta with a thick, rich meat ragu sauce
Prepare the sauce for the spaghetti Bolognese. To do this, peel the onion and garlic. Cut the onion in half, then dice it finely. Crush the garlic cloves with the flat side of a knife and chop them.
Pour olive oil into a large frying pan and heat it up. Add the chopped onion and garlic, and sauté over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned.
Add the minced meat to the onion and garlic, and cook in a frying pan over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring with a fork (to prevent lumps from forming).

Remove the seeds and membranes from the sweet pepper, then dice it into small cubes. Add it to the pan with the meat and sauté for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Make sure the pepper does not burn.

Peel the tomatoes and place them in a blender. Blend on high speed, then add the mixture to the pan with the meat and vegetables. Season with salt and pepper. Add herbs to taste and simmer the Bolognese sauce over low heat for 20 minutes.

Prepare the spaghetti. To do this, bring water to a boil in a large pot and add a little salt. Place the spaghetti into the water without breaking the strands; do this gradually, as the portion submerged in the water softens. Cook for 10 minutes.
Drain the cooked spaghetti in a colander. There’s no need to rinse it—this way, the pasta will bind better with the sauce. You can, however, add a tablespoon of olive oil.
Add the spaghetti to the Bolognese sauce and stir. Heat everything together in the pan. Then, divide into individual portions and sprinkle with grated cheese. Serve immediately.
A fluffy omelet with melted cheese, ready in 10 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the milk and a pinch of salt.
Melt the butter in a pan and pour in the egg mixture.
Sprinkle with grated cheese and fold the omelet in half.
